This review establishes no difficulty-setting semantics. The report itself correctly says byte-valued native branch input, so its factual claims do not need correction.

The symbolic memory model uses pointer identities and selected native write summaries rather than a byte-complete VM/tag/alias model. It also does not emulate native float compatibility adjustments. The independently checked write intervals and explicit non-overlap/stability/normal-return preconditions support these two prefixes; they must not be generalized automatically to other scripts, aliases, failures or reentrant native calls.
